summary: No blocking source defect found in the two new terminal postprocess scripts. The nine-table normal readout and terminal-only six-archive/seven-duplicate cleanup paths match the reviewed producers. No source fix is required. This is provisional source acceptance only; the active run, observer, intake, archive and metrics were not queried or executed.
reviewer_context: Continuation by the same delegated reviewer of the integrated deployment sources; not a claimed fresh-agent restart or cross-family review.

Only after terminal gates does the intake create the text tar manifest. A preexisting tar is rejected; local result/archive roots must also be absent, and D capacity must exceed the exact six-file expected bytes plus500MB.
The text archive is size/SHA checked, tar member names must equal the manifest, extraction uses filter=data, and every extracted text file is independently checked against its manifest.

For both exact controller run names, raw best_official_arrays.npz, states_raw normal_states.npz and best best.pth are copied to distinct D subdirectories and checked for exact size/SHA. All six archive entries must exist before invoking the stdlib analyzer and proceeding.

The analyzer is invoked with the current Python, -X utf8 -B -S and the exact local path; a nonzero exit stops intake. The376 source seals are checked again after analysis, before remote duplicate cleanup.

Cleanup builds its owned set from the six source-produced distinct binary paths plus this run text_intake.tar.gz. Source-derived representative path checking confirms exactly seven unique paths inside the owned run root and no overlap with the four protected references.

Before any remote unlink, every owned path must resolve inside ROOT and match size/SHA; original controller absence and all protected-four hashes are checked. Protected hashes are checked again after the exact loop of seven file unlinks. No recursive delete or historical-root cleanup is present.

After successful remote cleanup, only the local duplicate text tar is unlinked. All six unique D archives, including both selected best.pth files, are retained; archive markers point to their D paths. Future nonleader retirement requires the separate fresh result audit and is not implemented or authorized by this source review.

The new local command helper opens unique perstep stdout/stderr files, runs subprocess without check=True, writes actual started/ended times and child.returncode to a unique receipt, appends it to CAPTURES, and only then calls check_returncode.

This preserves primary stdout/stderr plus the actual exit255 receipt for the previously evidenced returned-scp255 failure path; failure is no longer raised before its return-code receipt is saved. A failed subprocess stops the sequence, so subsequent archive deletion is not reached.

No retry/fallback loop or extra try/except was added. Existing perstep capture files, the completed output receipt, local/archive roots and analysis output prevent implicit reruns/overwrite. Any later explicit recovery would need its own evidence and scope.

Each subprocess has a900-second timeout. The receipt is specifically for a subprocess that returns; launch/timeout exceptions leave their primary output files but do not synthesize a completed exit code. No universal failure-capture or successful-runtime claim is made.

The inherited transport module is used only for load/sha/OPTIONS. Its previously reviewed guarded import chain does not run its historical publishing main. The new intake uses its own capturing command helper for both SSH/scp and the analyzer.

expected_table_rows.group_metrics: All saved identity/camera/scene groups; variable count

limitations: Source PASS is not evidence that formal50, all10 child exits, the original observer, intake, six D archives, seven remote duplicate removals, normal analysis or paper acceptance have actually completed.

Only the original registered observer may run at the user-provided scheduled node; this review did not inspect training logs/status, GPU/PID/handle state, current session/native receipts, raw matrices or checkpoints and did not touch the observer.
The terminal-only time/COMPLETE/child/capacity/archive/protected-reference gates are future executable checks. Their actual truth is not inferred from source or planned timing.

The analyzer checks normal CSV metrics/CMC/groups and reuses verified producer state summaries plus selected comparisons. It is not a fresh installed-GT/NPZ/tensor integrity audit. Full independent result audit must precede local nonleader-best retirement.
Recorded runtime retained in analysis is the original evaluation-runtime field; teacher50+extra50 is a disclosed epoch budget, not equal compute or a newly measured end-to-end training time.

Returned subprocess failures, including the evidenced scp255 path, receive stdout/stderr/exit receipts before check_returncode. No receipt for an unreturned/timeout subprocess is fabricated, and no automatic retry or recovery is approved.

Schema matching is based on the actual reviewed source producers and a scheduling-key-name check; remote snippets were compiled with synthetic literal metadata only. No fabricated runtime artifact or fake completed result was created.
Requested gpt-6-astra/max routing is UNATTESTED. This follow-up semantic review remains same-family/provisional and makes no cross-family acceptance claim.
